hook.text: Corals grow annual bands like tree rings—each one recording the ocean's temperature and chemistry that year.

buildup.text: Scientists drill cores from massive corals—some living for centuries, others fossilized for millions of years.

discovery.text: Strontium-to-calcium ratios in coral bands reveal precise past sea surface temperatures—month by month.

twist.text: Coral records show that El Niño events have intensified since the 1970s compared to previous centuries.

climax.text: These records fill gaps where instruments didn't exist—extending our climate knowledge back thousands of years.

punchline.text: Corals keep diaries of the ocean's past—written in chemistry.

quiz.question: How do coral records reveal past temperatures?
options: Chemical ratios in annual growth bands
The size of the coral colony
